Code §§ 1786.40 and 1786.50 — if an investigative report was obtained before the ghosting without source advice; pleaded to reach discovery even if the § 290 count later fails on the report; Plaintiff confirms no 1786.40 advice arrived; 1786.52 discovery date does not appear on the face of the pleading

[AFFIRMATIVE FACT] Penal Code § 290.46(j) — last count on page one; Home Depot ran a background check; the report came back with § 290.46 registry information; Home Depot used that information to ghost Plaintiff and make an employment decision; taking those allegations as true, the claim is plausible; report not attached because Home Depot has not produced it
[OMITTED] Tameny / IIED — two-year CCP § 335.1 clock likely closed if the decision was August 2024; not the load-bearing claim

[PRESERVED, NOT PLEADED] FEHA and Fair Chance Act — no CRD right-to-sue in the record
key_facts: On or about August 2024, Plaintiff was hired to work at The Home Depot distribution/fulfillment center at 5395 Hopkins Road, Tracy, CA 95377. He accepted the position and began onboarding. Home Depot ran a background check. The report came back with information disclosed pursuant to Penal Code § 290.46, including Plaintiff's California Sex Offender Registry listing. Home Depot used that information, in whole or in part, to ghost him and make an employment decision. The claim is pleaded as Home Depot's own report and decision, not off the UPS/First Advantage report. No offer letter, time records, wage statements, vendor name, or adverse-action notice is in the portfolio. The complaint does not attach a Home Depot report because Home Depot has not produced it. Labor Code § 1198.5 inspection has not yet been demanded. Serve CSC, not the Tracy building.
procedural_status: Executed verified complaint and San Joaquin intake dated September 8, 2026; signed, not yet filed. The 290 count is now pleaded as Home Depot's own report (registry information in it) and Home Depot's use of that information to ghost Plaintiff — not off the UPS file. Serve CSC, not 5395 Hopkins Road. Do not bury Serrato disclosures that day.
damages: No wage rate or duration is in the record. Portfolio valuation is the post-favorable-MTD settlement range: $50,000 / $70,000 / $90,000. That assumes the pleading survives demurrer with the affirmative report-and-use facts taken as true. Do not import UPS/Pilot numbers. Contingent statutory remedies: Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A) actual/treble with a $250 floor, fees, exemplary damages, or a civil penalty capped at $25,000; ICRAA § 1786.50 actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater.
risk: The file still has no Home Depot offer, report, or notice. The complaint now alleges those report contents as fact. A demurrer must take them as true; Lerma cannot run without Home Depot's report in the record. If production later shows court records and no California-registry source, the 290 count dies then. Vendor still unnamed. ICRAA remains the backup path. CCP § 340(a) remains a defense argument on the civil-penalty piece. Tameny is omitted. Naming the Tracy building or serving the warehouse instead of CSC would be party/service defects.
evidence: Plaintiff's statement — hire on or about August 2024 at 5395 Hopkins Road, Tracy; accepted; began onboarding; Home Depot ran a background check; the report contained registry information; Home Depot used it to ghost him (no independent paper in the folder)
